payload.title: Wedding Destinations in March for Spring or Autumn Weddings
payload.excerpt: March is a shoulder month for a wedding abroad, so the question is which kind of shoulder you want. It is early spring in Europe and autumn in New Zealand, while Bali, Fiji, Mauritius and the Seychelles are still inside the wet, cyclone or monsoon season described for them by Smartraveller.
key_takeaways: The ten are the Greek islands, Lake Como, the Amalfi Coast, the French Riviera and Portugal in Europe's early spring, and New Zealand, Mauritius, the Seychelles, Bali and Fiji in the southern autumn and late summer.
In Europe, March nights are cool at every official station quoted here, so heating, wraps and an indoor room belong in the plan.
Fiji, Mauritius and the Seychelles are inside the cyclone or monsoon season Smartraveller describes for March, so a covered ceremony option and a buffer day are part of the booking.
Choose on the trade-off you can live with: cool evenings in Europe, a changeable autumn in New Zealand, or the wet, cyclone or monsoon season in the tropics.

faq.q: Is March a good month to get married?
faq.a: It can be, if you plan for a shoulder month: cool early spring in Europe, autumn in New Zealand, or warm, wet weeks in the tropics.

faq.q: Where is warm for a wedding in March?
faq.a: Mauritius and the Seychelles. Port Louis in Mauritius has a March mean daily maximum of 31.5°C in its 1971 to 2000 normals, and Victoria in the Seychelles has 31.2°C in its 1981 to 2010 normals. Both are wet too, so plan for heat and rain together.

faq.q: Which European destinations suit a March wedding?
faq.a: The Greek islands, Lake Como, the Amalfi Coast, the French Riviera and Portugal can all work, if your venue is open on your date and the plan allows for cool evenings and indoor space.

faq.q: Is March cyclone season in Fiji?
faq.a: Yes. As at November 2026, Smartraveller puts Fiji's cyclone season from November to April, and the Fiji Meteorological Service called March 2026 the wet season.

faq.q: Is March autumn in New Zealand?
faq.a: Yes. Earth Sciences New Zealand described March 2026 as a dry start to autumn for much of the country, a single year's reading rather than a long-term normal.
